text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Kuwait's economy has recovered well from the seven-month 1990-91 Iraqi occupation but the government still faces challenges, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) said.

- Iranian officials continuously confuse statements tailored for local consumption with those addressed to the international community. On Saturday, Iran warned that it was capable of blocking the Strait of Hormuz, the only entrance to the Gulf waterway.
- Communications Ministry to hold privatisation seminar on Wednesday. Kuwait plans to privatise public utilities including the telecommunications sector.
- Niger President Ibrahim Bare Mainassara arrives in Kuwait on official visit.
- Emir Sheikh Jaber al-Ahmad al-Sabah receives parliament speaker Ahmad al-Saadoun.
- Information Minister Sheikh Saud Nasser al-Sabah says the government does not want to clash with parliament.

- Finance Minister Nasser al-Rodhan says the government will not oblige the private sector to employ Kuwaitis. The government is considering several measures to encourge businesses to employ Kuwaitis.
- Kuwait Stock Exchange records highest trading volume. Some 455 million shares were traded on Monday.
- Kuwait Central Bank to go on the Internet with financial and banking information.
